templates_considered: RET-001: audit_log only written by audit function; fits the audit-control part of the ask. Used as-is with its own names.
AUTH-010 endpoints_need_login: fits the access part, but covers every endpoint; narrowed to PHI tables with a new key HIPAA-010 instead.
CONF-010 sensitive_tables_need_login: needs a phi table tag that does not exist; not used.
CONF-011 sensitive_fields_marked: right check, but the ask is PHI tables only; adapted into HIPAA-020 with a tables scope.
CONF-012 confidential_tables_tagged: needs tags to be added to tables; proposed in reply, not used.
CONF-013 views_hide_sensitive: no saved-view files found in the pull; not used, not checked further.
DATA-010 no_pii_in_responses: same idea as HIPAA-030 but the template uses fields without table scoping; I used db.output_fields_forbidden with patients.* names.
LOG-001 no_sensitive_data_in_logs: right idea; adapted into HIPAA-050 with a tables scope and debug.log only.
RET-002 retained_data_cleaned_up: needs a retained tag on tables; no tags exist; not used.
AUTH-020 own_records_only: patients have no owner field to constrain on; did not fit.
VND-001 approved_vendors_only: needs an approved vendor list from the customer; not used.
SEC-014 tokens_expire: relevant to automatic logoff, but the token setting is not in a statement I could find; not used.
SEC-012, CHG-001, CONV-023 and others: outside the PHI ask or need tags; not used.

rules.covers: access control: PHI endpoints require login
PHI identifiers and clinical text marked sensitive
minimum necessary: patient reads do not fetch SSN or insurance ID
audit controls: PHI access calls the audit function
no request input (PHI) written to logs
audit controls: the audit log table exists
audit controls: only the audit function writes audit records

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Role-based access to PHI beyond login (least privilege)
Retention periods and cleanup for PHI
Encryption at rest and in transit, backups, automatic logoff, emergency access
Business associate agreements, risk analysis, workforce training, breach notification
Tagging PHI tables as phi so rules can use tags
Which vendors may receive patient data
Audit log content (who read which PHI) beyond the audit call

assumptions: patients, appointments and clinical_notes are the PHI tables; the customer named them.
record_audit_event is the audit function; audit_log is the audit table.
tables scope on object and table checks selects objects that reach the named tables directly or through functions, as the skill describes.
The sensitive attribute is the one table.field_attribute_required reads with attribute and value true.
A name-based scope is acceptable now because the workspace has no PHI tags; the customer may add tags later.
confusions: The skill says to start from a template when one fits, but AUTH-010 fits only if scoped to PHI tables; it was unclear whether to keep the template key with a narrowed scope or use a new key. I used HIPAA-010.

The skill says scope params go at the top level of params, but nothing says whether they can sit alongside a check's own params in the same params object; parse accepted it, but I could not confirm the rule matches what I intended without evaluate.

table.field_attribute_required lists field_names+ and field_types+ as 'must set at least one', while the description says if both are set both must match; the '+' marker is ambiguous, so I set only field_names.
The pulled table files show no sensitive attribute on any field, so I could not tell how a sensitive flag is written in the pulled XanoScript; the attribute check may flag every listed field.
Tables have no tags in the pull, and the skill says to scope by tag, not name; there is no guidance on what to do when the tag does not yet exist beyond proposing it.
The 'where values go' guidance covers debug.log but says nothing about whether logging a whole variable (not request input) counts as a leak; I kept HIPAA-050 to request input only.
No check tells whether an endpoint reads PHI versus writes it, so HIPAA-040 applies the audit call to reads and writes alike; the skill does not say whether that is intended.
wished_for: A HIPAA or PHI starting bundle (templates for PHI tables, audit calls and minimum-necessary fields) with worked examples of tables scope.
A recipe for adding a tag to a table and then scoping rules by it, in the workspace-change flow.
A check that reads whether an endpoint is read-only versus writing, so audit rules can target reads or writes.
A check for role or least-privilege access to a named table.
An example of the XanoScript form of a sensitive field, so the pulled files can be checked against the attribute check.
why_confidence: Six policies parse with no rule warnings, and the PHI-table rules probably flag the real gaps (public appointments endpoint, PHI logging, unaudited PHI access, returned SSN). But HIPAA is mostly outside what a policy can check: encryption, BAAs, training, retention and role-based access are not covered. I did not run policy evaluate, so the findings are predictions. The name-based scopes and the untested sensitive attribute check could also miss or over-match.
